# [PR #14231] [#14125][fix] Auto-disable kv_cache_config.enable_block_reuse for multimodal models

source: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/14231
state: open | updated: 2026-09-26T04:06:03Z
labels: Community want to contribute

## 正文

Fixes #14125. The prefix-block hash does not yet include the multimodal embedding hash, so the second identical multimodal request hits a stale cached prefix and fails with the Multimodal token count mismatch error, after which the server stops accepting traffic. This change detects multimodal models at LLM init time using the existing input processor registry and flips kv_cache_config.enable_block_reuse to False, while leaving any explicit user setting alone so the opt-in path via extra_llm_api_options keeps working. Unit tests cover the default-flip, explicit-on, text-only, and none-config branches of the helper.

## Walkthrough

This PR addresses a bug where multimodal models with default KV cache block reuse enabled fail on subsequent requests with token count mismatches. A new helper function detects multimodal input processors and automatically disables block reuse (unless explicitly set), preventing cache collisions. The helper integrates into model initialization and includes four test cases validating default disable, explicit enable, text-only passthrough, and None config handling.

## Changes

**Multimodal KV Cache Block Reuse Prevention**

|Layer / File(s)|Summary|
|---|---|
|**Block reuse disable helper and model build integration** <br> `tensorrt_llm/llmapi/llm.py`|`_maybe_disable_block_reuse_for_multimodal` checks if the input processor is multimodal and `enable_block_reuse` is enabled by default (not explicitly set), then logs a warning and disables block reuse to prevent cache key collisions. The helper is called in `_TorchLLM._build_model()` immediately after input processor setup.|
|**Block reuse disable helper tests** <br> `tests/unittest/llmapi/test_llm.py`|Four test cases validate that the helper: flips `enable_block_reuse` from default True to False for multimodal processors, respects explicitly-set `enable_block_reuse=True`, leaves text-only processors unchanged, and safely handles None config arguments. Includes two fake processor classes to mock multimodal and text-only behavior.|

🎯 2 (Simple) | ⏱️ ~12 minutes

</details>
